assumptions: Star activity follows REBASE's rule: a site differing from the recognition site at one base.
limits: These are possible sites, not cuts: they need non-standard conditions, and the list says nothing about their rate.
bio.jane/contract.question: Where else could these enzymes cut this molecule under star conditions, by REBASE's star-activity list and its one-base rule?

description: Where the given enzymes could ALSO cut the open plasmid under non-standard conditions, from REBASE's own star-activity list and its one-base rule. Not cut sites: these need low ionic strength, high pH, Mn²⁺ for Mg²⁺, glycerol, DMSO or some detergents, and are what turns an over-digested reaction into a band pattern that reads as the wrong clone.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

enzymes.description: enzymes to check — resolved against the bundled cut catalog (REBASE spellings; smaller than the REBASE dossier the editor shows). Left unset, the run uses your active enzyme collection.

name: find_star_sites

enzymes.description: per enzyme: whether REBASE examined it, and its possible star sites here

sites.description: total possible star sites across the enzymes REBASE has examined

unexamined.description: how many of the enzymes REBASE has NOT tested for star activity
